newsitem.title: USA: Dakota Mining, USMX to merge.
newsitem.headline: Dakota Mining, USMX to merge.

text.p: Dakota Mining Corp and USMX Inc said Monday they agreed in principle to merge.
Under terms of the deal, USMX shareholders will get one Dakota common share for every 1.1 common shares of USMX.
Dakota said Pegasus Gold Inc, which holds about 30 percent of USMX outstanding common, agreed in principle to support the deal.
The company said the merger will make it a mid-sized gold producer of about 140,000 ounces annually in 1997, growing to 200,000 ounces in 1998.
Dakota said its president and chief executive, Alan Bell, will be president and chief executive of the new company, and USMX president and chief executive, Donald Bellum, will be board chairman.
Dakota closed Friday at 1-1/2. Trading was delayed pending the news. USMX closed at 1-27/32.
Dakota said the combined company will have significant cash resources and opportunities to expand reserves on existing properties. It also will pursue other acquisitions, Dakota said.

Separately, Dakata said USMX will need about $12.1 million more to achieve production at its Illinois Creek gold mine in Alaska. The company also needs another several million dollars to comply with financial covenants of the project, Dakota said.
Dakota said it will use proceeds from a private placement of special warrants to achieve production at the mine.
